headline: The program's single biggest exposure is Vendor data feed contracts (Ops): it sits on the critical path, is already blocked, and 15 downstream tasks across 5 teams can't start until it clears.

risks.why_it_matters: This is the one task where a delay doesn't just slip its own deadline: it stalls the ingestion pipeline, data validation, and everything downstream of those. It has no float, so every day it stays blocked comes straight off the launch date.
risks.mitigation: Escalate the vendor contract to legal for expedited review this week, and assign Ops a backup data source so Engineering isn't fully blocked on a single vendor's timeline.

risks.why_it_matters: Currently 40% complete and behind pace for its elapsed time. Four workstreams wait on this one API layer: audit logging, the dashboard front-end, analytics tagging, and the security pen test.
risks.mitigation: Pull one engineer off T29 (accessibility review, not time-critical yet) onto the reporting API for the next week.

risks.why_it_matters: Already complete, but it is the root of the entire dependency tree. Worth flagging only because a late-discovered gap here would be the most expensive possible rework.
risks.mitigation: No action needed now. Treat any new requirement as a change request against the frozen spec rather than an edit to T01.

cascade_summary: If Vendor data feed contracts slips 3 more days, the program end date moves from day 41 to day 44, a 3-day hit that lands on Compliance, Data, Engineering, Marketing and Ops.

T06.mitigation: Have S. Ibarra build against a mocked feed now, so the pipeline is ready to switch to live data the day the contract signs.

T19.mitigation: Confirm the filing window with J. Okafor now and draft the submission in parallel with reconciliation, not after it.
